title: Multi-Cloud Egress Cost Comparison

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.4.27 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.4.27 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`aws:billing` collected via Billing exports (CUR, Cost Management export, BigQuery billing); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Billing exports (CUR, Cost Management export, BigQuery billing)
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:billing" ( OR sourcetype="azure:cost" OR sourcetype="gcp:billing")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.27_multi_cloud_egress_cost_27"
| sort -_time
description: Egress drives surprise bills; comparing outbound spend by provider and region guides data locality and CDN decisions.
value: Detecting multi-cloud egress cost comparison early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Map each provider’s line items to normalized `usage_type` and `cost` fields during ingestion. Join with application tags where available. Alert on week-over-week egress growth above threshold per provider.
visualization: Line chart (egress USD by provider), Bar chart (region), Table (top services driving egress).
knownFalsePositives: Cloud billing and cost files often arrive a day or more late, include credits and refunds, and use tags that do not line up with app names, so a spike is not always a real overrun. We narrow alerts to sustained trends and we exclude test or sandbox projects when we can.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure Billing exports (CUR, Cost Management export, BigQuery billing) with the modular input for `aws:billing`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Map each provider’s line items to normalized `usage_type` and `cost` fields during ingestion. Join with application tags where available. Alert on week-over-week egress growth above threshold per provider.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:billing" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:billing" ( OR sourcetype="azure:cost" OR sourcetype="gcp:billing")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.27_multi_cloud_egress_cost_27"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:billing` in `index=cloud` to detect multi-cloud egress cost comparison. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_27_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (egress USD by provider), Bar chart (region), Table (top services driving egress)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Billing exports (CUR, Cost Management export, BigQuery billing) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of multi-cloud egress cost comparison so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
